title: Four bird drought samples had observation sensitivity thresholds from 1.115 to 4.668 under a multiplicative model
abstract: We tested how a bounded observation change can alter the sign of a bird abundance response to drought. Four study samples from a 2024 release supplied 88 rows for 60 species units with positive drought and reference means. Under a multiplicative observation model, exact bounds on the mean log true ratio equal the recorded mean plus or minus the log of an allowed factor. The smallest factor that permits zero ranged from 1.115 in Spain to 4.668 in North Dakota. A factor of 1.25 left three mean bounds below zero. These are sensitivity measures for fixed source means, not estimates of actual bias or confidence intervals. Two other samples lacked means. Zero means excluded 18 species. Different protocols, selected species, sampling error and shared events limit inference. The samples permit geographic checks but no balanced independent-period test. No air pollution effect or causal climate effect was tested. The package gives code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Conditional plug-in bounds at observation factor 1.25 and fractions of selected species with negative signs fixed by larger factors. These are not confidence intervals.
